The '''1954 Hastings Broncos football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented [[Hastings College]] as a member of the [[Nebraska College Conference]] (NCC) during the [[1954 college football season]]. In their sixth season under head coach [[Tom McLaughlin (American football)|Tom McLaughlin]], the Broncos compiled a perfect 9–0 record (7–0 in conference games), won the NCC championship, defeated [[1954 College of Emporia Fighting Presbies football team|College of Emporia]] in the [[Mineral Water Bowl]], and outscored opponents by a total of 230 to 97.<ref name=LS/><ref>{{cite web|title=1954 Football Team|publisher=Hastings College|accessdate=March 21, 2024|url=https://www.hastingsbroncos.com/assets/Hall_of_Fame/Hall_of_Fame_Members/1954_Football_Team}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Final NCC Standings |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/40703748/the_lincoln_star/ |newspaper=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |location=[[Lincoln, Nebraska]] |date=November 8, 1954 |page=8 |access-date=December 17, 2019 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref>

Five Hastings players were selected as first-team players on the 1954 NCC all-conference team: Lavon Eisenhauer at end; Veryl Borden at guard; Gene Fleharty at tackle; Chuck Stickels at quarterback; and Bruce Edwards at halfback.  Two others were named to the second team: Hilly Beck at the end and Ladd Cochrane at the back.  Guard Jim Sterp received an honorable mention.<ref name=allncc>{{cite news|title=All NCC: Hastings Heads NCC Eleven; League Champs Earn Five All-Star Berths|newspaper=The Lincoln Star|author=Forrest Miller and Glenn Speidel|date=November 14, 1954|page=16|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-lincoln-star-all-ncc-hastings-heads/143815071/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

The team played home games at A. H. Jones Stadium in [[Hastings, Nebraska]].
